bull_case: AI expands TAM while buybacks amplify per-share cash flow growth.
bear_case: If AI spend becomes defensive and growth slows, high reinvestment may earn lower incremental returns.
thesis: Adobe combines high cash conversion with low capital intensity and large buybacks. H1 owner-style FCF after PP&E and SBC is roughly $4.0B, while Q3 added $2.52B OCF. The remaining question is whether AI-related R&D keeps producing ARR growth rather than merely defending the installed base.

evidence.claim: H1 OCF was $5.123B and PP&E purchases only $95M.
H1 repurchases were $4.589B; Q3 added ~9.5M shares repurchased.

counterevidence: AI lowers content-creation barriers and could shift value from application vendors toward models, distribution layers or new agentic workflows.
unknowns: Long-run AI monetization per user, Firefly inference economics, and how much AI-first ARR is incremental versus bundled/reclassified ARR.
falsifiers: If ARR growth falls to low single digits while AI usage rises, or owner FCF/share stops compounding despite buybacks, the moat/compounder thesis is downgraded.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Strong cash generation and low capital intensity rebut structural incremental-ROIC collapse.
Share count is shrinking, not persistently diluting.

next_checks: Q4/FY2026 ARR, AI-first ARR, OCF, SBC, repurchases, share count and Digital Media/Experience growth

subscores.rationale: High software margins and low physical capex support strong incremental cash returns.
R&D, AI products, document productivity and Experience Cloud provide multiple reinvestment paths.
OCF is strong, capex low and aggressive repurchases reduce shares outstanding materially.
